name: inprocess-cva6-axi4-timer-f1-rv64
notes: Real RV64I execution on the same one packed AXI4 CVA6, the same PULP timer and the same host RAM. The F1 program slot executes 1..4 true RV64I words from the declared subset (LUI, ADDI, ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, ADDIW, ADDW, SLLIW, SRLIW, SRAIW, and LD/SD against x18 inside the 64-byte data window); the retirement trace, the reference values and the case-line fields are 64-bit, and the trace hash is FNV-1a 64. This is not the low-32 projection of the RV32 scenario: an ADDIW/ADDW/SRLIW writeback is compared as the sign-extended 64-bit value the RVFI record carries.

The subset is straight-line and read-after-write: a word may read only a register this same program wrote earlier, or x0/x18, so the reference trace is decided by the declared state and not by firmware state. No branch, jump, CSR, system, compressed, floating-point, atomic or RV64-compressed word is admitted, and no register the firmware owns (x8/x9/x18) may be written.
Ten generated programs were submitted as fixed records in one run (the closed-loop F1 fuzzer is RV32-only and is not claimed here). F5 stays refused by name: the AXI4 host holds irq_i low.
